originalTitle: Machine could make more donated lungs suitable for transplant
summary: Nice backs wider use of system that keeps organs alive outside the body, to help improve low transplantation rates
content: A machine that keeps organs alive outside the body could save four in every five donated lungs that currently go to waste in England and Wales. The UK has one of the poorest lung transplantation rates in the world. The latest figures from NHS Blood and Transplant show that 170 patients in the UK, including six children, are waiting for new lungs. Most adults wait a year for a transplant and some wait two years or more. Up to a fifth of adults awaiting an urgent transplant die within a year of joining the transplant list, before a suitable lung is found. But only 23% of all donated lungs are used, with donated lungs sometimes declined not only because of organ quality but due to staffing and theatre capacity issues. Draft guidance from the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (Nice) recommends that the XVIVO perfusion system be used in the NHS for a four-year period to assess its effectiveness and value for money. Nice estimates that the machine could help rescue four in five donated lungs that are currently unused, by helping them remain viable for transplantation, which could unlock hundreds of organs for transplants. The machine warms donated lungs to body temperature and pumps a fluid through them that mimics blood plasma, while also ventilating them to mimic normal breathing. This allows transplant teams to monitor how the lungs are functioning, treat infection, drain excess fluid and reinflate collapsed areas. While the machine has been trialled at three adult transplant centres, until now Nice had not endorsed the technique in all transplant centres or approved its use in paediatric cases. Nice says the draft guidance aims to ensure all transplant centres can benefit from the technology, regardless of their size or location. Dr Anastasia Chalkidou, the healthtech programme director at Nice, said the machine should allow more lungs to remain available for transplantation that otherwise would be discarded. “Every donated lung is a precious gift, and right now too many of them never reach a patient who needs them,” she said. “This technology has the potential to change that, giving transplant teams the time and information they need to make the most of organs that would otherwise go unused.” Chalkidou said the move reflected wider efforts to improve access “so that where a patient is treated no longer determines whether they can benefit from a transplant”. Jonathan Blades, the head of policy at Asthma + Lung UK, said: “Lung transplant rates in the UK remain lower than in many other developed countries, while respiratory health outcomes remain the worst in Europe. Renewed political and research focus is needed to transform lung health in the UK, and this new technology marks an important step towards that ambition. “We look forward to seeing the results of this trial, which could give more people with serious lung conditions more precious time with their loved ones. It could also reduce the number of donated lungs that currently go to waste if they are unsuitable for transplantation.” Prof Andrew Fisher, a member of the British Transplantation Society and a consultant transplant physician at Newcastle upon Tyne hospitals NHS foundation trust, said: “It’s important that robust evidence is generated that shows exactly how much impact the use of this device has on lung transplant activity and supports timely access to transplant for patients desperately waiting for a suitable organ.”
chineseTitle: 机器可以使更多捐赠的肺适合移植
chineseSummary: 尼斯支持更广泛地使用使器官在体外存活的系统，以帮助改善低移植率
chineseContent: 在英格兰和威尔士，一台让器官在体外保持活力的机器可以挽救五分之四的捐赠肺部，这些肺部目前已经被浪费了。英国是世界上肺移植率最差的国家之一。 NHS血液和移植部门的最新数据显示，英国有170名患者（其中包括六名儿童）正在等待新肺。大多数成年人等待移植一年，有些则等待两年或更长时间。多达五分之一等待紧急移植的成年人在加入移植名单后一年内、在找到合适的肺之前死亡。但所有捐献肺中只有 23% 得到使用，捐献肺有时会下降，不仅因为器官质量，还因为人员配备和手术室容量问题。国家健康与护理卓越研究所（尼斯）的指南草案建议 NHS 使用 XVIVO 灌注系统四年，以评估其有效性和性价比。尼斯估计，该机器可以帮助挽救目前未使用的五分之四的捐赠肺部，帮助它们保持移植活力，从而释放数百个器官进行移植。该机器将捐献的肺部加热至体温，并泵入模拟血浆的液体，同时为它们通气以模拟正常呼吸。这使得移植团队能够监测肺部的功能、治疗感染、排出多余的液体并使塌陷的区域重新膨胀。虽然该机器已在三个成人移植中心进行了试用，但到目前为止，尼斯尚未在所有移植中心认可该技术或批准其在儿科病例中使用。尼斯表示，该指南草案旨在确保所有移植中心都能从该技术中受益，无论其规模或位置如何。 Anastasia Chalkidou 博士
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
